rationale:
Evidence across iterations 0 to 3 is consistent. All 180 trials ended off track with no finishes. Each run had exactly one line-loss event, max_error sat at the 0.06 m limit, progress stayed at 0.10 to 0.17, and steering oscillation stayed low (0.07 to 0.15). Gains are not the limiting factor. The best score so far is iteration 1 (62.18: ki 0.4, kp 2.5, kd 0.2, base_speed 1.4, outer sensors at +/-0.03 m). Iteration 2 (ki 1.0) scored 59.93. Iteration 3 (outer sensors widened to +/-0.045 m, ki 1.0) scored 56.65, which is worse, so the wider array did not fix the failure and may have hurt slightly. Reading the feedback on that candidate, the evaluator also flagged that the geometry field did not match the rationale. The ambiguity is resolved by reverting to the narrower array.

What I change: nothing relative to the best-scoring iteration 1 build. Geometry returns to the +/-0.03 m array (outer) and +/-0.015 m (inner), so the build is unambiguous. Controller stays at ki 0.4, kp 2.5, kd 0.2, base_speed 1.4, line_loss last_direction, with weights [2, 1, 0, -1, -2]. I am deliberately not changing line_loss or base_speed in this final race of the iteration. An untested change could lose the approval, and no run has finished, so there is no completion_time evidence to justify a speed change.

Expected result: about the iteration 1 score (roughly 60 to 62), with progress near 0.17 and one line-loss event per run. Hypotheses for the next iteration: (a) the line is lost once early because of the start transient or the first sharp bend, not from a steady offset; (b) line_loss=search_right against last_direction may change the recovery; (c) if completion does occur, completion_time decides whether base_speed should rise toward 1.5 to 1.6. Measurements to watch: progress and line_loss_events per track, max_error and where in the run it occurs, completion_time, and steering_oscillation.
